title: Why Low Gears Make Hills Easier

scenes.text: You start up a hill, and suddenly your legs burn and the pedals feel like concrete. Almost every new rider has been there.
Here is what a lower gear does. Each pedal turn moves the bike a shorter distance, so every push takes less force from your legs.
The trade is speed. You turn the pedals more often to cover the same road, but it is an effort you can sustain.
Shift before the hill starts, while you are still pedaling lightly. Changing gears under heavy pressure is rough on the chain.
